name: Disclosure costs

subjectOf.text: Increased disclosure obligations let so-called pilot fish emulate hedge funds' investment strategies and positions, which makes those positions more expensive to build and strips systematic bargaining strength from the negotiation process.
subjectOf.abstract: disclosure obligations, "pilot fish" can increasingly emulate investment strategies and positions. As a result, investment positions can become more expensive and systematic bargaining strength is removed from the negotiation process.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463
scope_conditions: markets where competitors can observe and copy disclosed positions

subjectOf.text: There is a real risk that increased disclosure through Form PF would destroy the balance of power in the restructuring process.
subjectOf.abstract: In summary, there is a real risk that increased disclosures via Form PF would destroy the balance of power in the restructuring process.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463
scope_conditions: if Form PF data were introduced into the bankruptcy process

subjectOf.text: Using a regression discontinuity design around the 150 million dollar registration threshold with five years of performance data on more than 3500 reporting private funds, the study finds no significant effect of Dodd-Frank requirements on private fund performance, with all p-values above the 5 percent level.
subjectOf.abstract: Using an array of robustness tests validating the RD results, the paper shows that the requirements introduced by the Dodd-Frank Act create no significant effect on private fund performance. The P-values for all RD results are above the 5% level and confirm the finding of no affect.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097
scope_conditions: private funds reporting performance data, 2010 to 2015
regression discontinuity around the $150 million AUM registration threshold
